evals.name: kafka-proposed-for-notifications
evals.prompt: Checkout is blocking on MSG91 (see INC-231). Rahul wants to bring in Kafka for the SMS and email notifications. Is that the right call or is there something better for us? Someone also asked whether we should move to GKE while we're at it. I want this settled and written down.
evals.expected_output: The messaging choice is laid out with Kafka shown next to lighter options, one recommendation that fits the repository's facts (about 300 checkouts a minute at peak, which is 5 SMS a second, three developers and no ops engineer, Postgres and Cloud Run already decided) with the condition that would flip it, and the claim in INC-231 that Kafka's exactly-once delivery would stop duplicate SMS is corrected: the guarantee ends at Kafka and does not cover the call to MSG91. The design is one an expert would sign: the notification is enqueued atomically with the order, the worker runs in a way Cloud Run supports, a timed-out MSG91 send is not blindly retried into a duplicate SMS (the vendor notes say there is no idempotency key), a message past the 6 hour window has a defined end that no sweep undoes, and the backlog left by an outage is drained under MSG91's 20 requests a second limit so the sender ID is not suspended. The GKE question is answered from ADR 0002 without reopening or re-recording it, and one new adr-tools style ADR 0003 in docs/adr/ has status Proposed, since nobody answered; the final message says the choice still awaits the user. Nothing is recorded for what the repository already settles, no second index or catalogue of ADRs is started, no code is changed and nothing is committed.
expectations: The reply or ADR 0003 compares Kafka with at least two other ways to take notifications out of the request (for example a Postgres outbox table with a worker, Cloud Pub/Sub or Cloud Tasks, RabbitMQ), giving each at least one strength and one cost

Exactly one option is recommended for the notification queue, it is not Kafka, and its reasons cite at least two facts from the repository: the peak of 300 checkouts a minute (docs/product/PRD.md 7.1), the three developers with no operations engineer (PRD 7.2 or ADR 0002), PostgreSQL already in use (ADR 0001), or GCP and Cloud Run already chosen (ADR 0002 or .bearing/company.json)

The final message or ADR 0003 (not only some other file) states a concrete condition under which Kafka or another option would become the better choice (for example replay, several independent consumers, or a much higher message volume)

The run answers the claim in docs/incidents/INC-231.md that Kafka's exactly-once delivery would stop duplicate SMS: it says the guarantee covers reads and writes inside Kafka, not the HTTP call to MSG91, so Kafka would not by itself satisfy PRD 4.2 and a duplicate guard is still needed whichever option is chosen; a reply that repeats or leaves the claim unchallenged does not pass

It recognises that retrying an MSG91 send that timed out can deliver a second SMS, because the send API has no idempotency key and a timed-out request may already have been delivered (docs/vendors/msg91.md), and says how the design handles that case against PRD 4.2 (for example keeping MSG91's request_id and checking the delivery report before resending, not resending an ambiguous timeout automatically, or stating the residual risk and who accepts it); a dedupe key on the queue alone does not pass

The design caps the rate at which SMS are sent to MSG91 below its limit of 20 requests a second (docs/vendors/msg91.md), so the backlog built up while MSG91 was down is not sent all at once when it recovers (for example a Cloud Tasks queue rate limit, a bounded worker concurrency, or a drain batch size with its arithmetic); retries with backoff alone do not pass

The design says what happens to a confirmation still undelivered when PRD 4.3's 6 hour retry window ends (for example marked failed, alerted or reported to support), not only that it is retried, and any sweep or re-enqueue job it describes skips rows past that window rather than sending them again

The recommendation says where the notification work runs on Cloud Run in a way consistent with ADR 0002's note that long-running background work does not fit a request-scoped instance (for example Cloud Tasks pushing to an HTTP handler, a separate worker service with CPU always allocated, or a scheduled Cloud Run job draining an outbox); a goroutine started by the checkout request and left running after the response does not pass

The design says how a confirmation is kept from being lost when the order commits but the enqueue fails, or the reverse: the notification is written in the same database transaction as the order (store.PlaceOrder), or the run names this gap and how it is closed; enqueueing after the commit with no answer for a failed enqueue does not pass

Every rate or number the run states is correct against the repository: 300 checkouts a minute is 5 SMS a second (10 messages a second counting email), 20 a minute is about one every 3 seconds, and ADR 0002's revisit condition is quoted as many services or stateful workloads Cloud Run cannot host; an invented or miscalculated figure presented as fact fails

The final message names the messaging option it recommends and says, in any wording, that the choice has not been made by the user yet and still awaits their decision; it does not present the choice as settled
No record written by the run (ADR, log, or other file) says the user, Rahul, the team or any named person chose or accepted the messaging option, since nobody answered

The GKE question is answered by citing ADR 0002 (Cloud Run) and naming what new fact would justify revisiting it, and docs/adr/0002-run-on-cloud-run.md is unchanged with no ADR, log entry or ADR section recording a decision about GKE or Cloud Run (a one-line cross-reference to ADR 0002 inside ADR 0003 is acceptable)

Exactly one new ADR file exists, at docs/adr/0003-<kebab title>.md, in the existing adr-tools shape (a '# 3. <title>' heading, a Date line, and Status, Context, Decision and Consequences sections) with its Status section saying Proposed, not Accepted

No second ADR directory, numbering scheme or catalogue of the ADRs was started beside docs/adr/ (for example docs/architecture/decisions.md or docs/decisions.md listing ADRs 0001 and 0002), and nothing was recorded for PostgreSQL or anything else the repository already settles

If ADR 0003 exists, it records Kafka among the options with the reason it was not chosen, and names at least one cost or piece of new work the chosen option brings (for example a worker to run, a retry schedule for the 6 hour window in PRD 4.3, or a table to purge)
No Go source file or go.mod was changed and no file was created or changed outside docs/ (for example no planning scaffold, notes directory, migration or config file)
The run made no git commit and did not push: the branch head is the same commit it started on
No file written or edited contains an em dash character

evals.name: search-change-against-recorded-decisions
evals.prompt: Search is killing us, almost a quarter of searches come back empty (numbers are in docs/metrics). I'm thinking we move to Elasticsearch. And should we put Redis in front of the catalogue page while we're at it? Decide and record it please.
evals.expected_output: Elasticsearch is weighed against lighter typo-tolerant options using the repository's numbers (180,000 products, two developers, AWS managed-first) and the breakdown of the zero-result sample: misspellings are 58% of it, so typo tolerance can at best remove about 13% of all searches; the 13% of Hindi or regional words are synonyms that no fuzzy matcher (Postgres or Elasticsearch) finds, and the 29% of unstocked products and other queries leave about 7% zero results whatever is chosen. One recommendation with its flip condition, the database load of a Postgres-based fix weighed against the load test's 85% CPU, and a missing fact raised as a question with the assumption stated. The Redis question is answered from ADR-003 and the 140 ms seven-day production p95: the 360 ms sale-hour figure is production but one hour, not the week the trigger names, and the 320 ms load test is staging; the connection opened per request is the cheaper fix, without adding a cache or editing ADR-003. The decision is recorded as ADR-005 in docs/decisions/ in the repository's own format with status Proposed, since nobody answered, and ADR-004 is not marked superseded while ADR-005 is only proposed. No code is changed and nothing is committed.
expectations: The run works out from docs/metrics/search-2026-09.md that fixing misspellings can at best remove about 13% of all searches from the zero-result set (23% x 58%) and states the zero-result rate that would remain (about 10% after typo tolerance alone, or about 7% if the Hindi and regional words are also handled), using it for the expected outcome or the flip condition rather than promising to fix the 23%

The run recognises that the 13% of zero-result queries that are Hindi or regional words for products listed under English names ('chappal', 'tawa') are not misspellings: neither pg_trgm similarity nor Elasticsearch fuzziness matches them, they need a synonym list or similar, and it says whether and how the recommendation covers them

Elasticsearch (or OpenSearch) is compared with at least one lighter option that handles typos (pg_trgm or fuzzy matching in the existing Postgres, Meilisearch, Typesense, or a hosted service such as Algolia), each with a strength and a cost
Exactly one search option is recommended, and its reasons cite at least one of: the 180,000 product catalogue size, the two-developer team, or ADR-002's managed-first rule

A concrete condition that would flip the search recommendation is stated (for example a zero-result rate that stays above the computed residual after the change, a latency limit, or a need such as synonyms at scale or facets)

The run names at least one fact the repository does not give that would change the search recommendation (for example budget for a hosted service, who would operate a new search service, or whether catalogue data may leave AWS) and either asks it or states the assumption it made about it

If the search recommendation keeps search in the existing Postgres (pg_trgm or similar), it names the load test's 85% peak RDS CPU (docs/metrics/loadtest-2026-08.md) and says how the extra query load is bounded or checked (for example running the fuzzy query only when full-text returns nothing, measuring it before release, or naming database load as a flip condition); a fallback design that never mentions the measured database load does not pass

The Redis question is answered from ADR-003's trigger (production p95 of GET /catalogue above 300 ms for a week) against the seven-day production p95 of 140 ms, and the answer is not to add a cache now; the 320 ms in docs/metrics/loadtest-2026-08.md is read as a staging test at 5x traffic on smaller hardware

The Redis answer addresses the 360 ms production sale-hour p95 in docs/metrics/search-2026-09.md: it is a real production figure above 300 ms, but for one hour, not the week ADR-003's trigger names, so it does not reopen ADR-003 by itself; the answer says what it does suggest (for example sale-day load on the connection-per-request path) rather than ignoring it or treating it as the trigger firing

The Redis answer names a cheaper cause visible in the repository to address before any cache: api.py opens a new Postgres connection on every request (the load test shows 410 new connections a second), so connection pooling comes before a cache

docs/decisions/ADR-003-no-cache-until-measured.md is unchanged (no appended review or revisit note), and no ADR, ADR section or decision-log entry records a decision on the cache; a one-line cross-reference to ADR-003 inside ADR-005 is acceptable

Exactly one new ADR file exists, at docs/decisions/ADR-005-<kebab title>.md, matching the existing ADRs (a title line 'ADR-005: ...', a 'Status:' line, and Context, Decision and Consequences sections) with its Status line saying Proposed, not Accepted
Nothing was created under docs/adr/, docs/architecture/ or any other new directory, and no index or catalogue of the ADRs was started beside docs/decisions/
No record written by the run (ADR, log, or other file) says the user or any named person chose or accepted the search option, since nobody answered
The final message names the recommended search option and says, in any wording, that it still awaits the user's decision; it does not present the choice as settled

ADR-004 is unchanged: its Status line is not changed to superseded or amended and its Decision section is not edited while ADR-005 is only Proposed; if the chosen option replaces Postgres full-text search, ADR-005 says it would supersede ADR-004 once accepted
If ADR-005 exists, it records Elasticsearch among the alternatives with the reason for accepting or rejecting it
No Python source file, pyproject.toml or migration was changed, no Redis, cache code, dependency or infrastructure was added, and no file was created or changed outside docs/
The run made no git commit and did not push: the branch head is the same commit it started on
No number about search or the catalogue is stated as measured unless it appears in the repository, and every share the run derives from the metrics is arithmetically right
No file written or edited contains an em dash character
